steps.text: Whisk brown sugar, orange juice, and honey together in a bowl until evenly combined. Use to glaze a fully cooked ham during the last 30 minutes of baking.

raw_recipe.headline: Classic Ham Glaze
raw_recipe.description: This easy ham glaze combines brown sugar, honey, and orange juice for a sweet, citrusy finish on holiday ham—and it’s ready in just five minutes.
raw_recipe.name: Classic Ham Glaze

recipeInstructions.text: Whisk brown sugar, orange juice, and honey together in a bowl until evenly combined. Use to glaze a fully cooked ham during the last 30 minutes of baking.

review.reviewBody: Excellent! I added a tablespoon of cinnamon to it and the kids love it!

Before putting on the glaze I rubbed the ham with maple syrup and brown sugar. I basted the ham every half hour. With a 1/2 hour left I heated the glaze until it thickened. I wish I would of done that from the start to have it stick a little better to the ham. The flavor was great.

I'm not a huge fan of ham but WOW! This is the only way I will.ever prepare a ham again. I used a spiral sliced ham instead of a whole ham. I also doubled the glaze and warmed it in a saucepan to help the sugar dissolve before basting each slice of ham. After about an hour in the oven, I basted the slces again. It took some time but well worth it. Honey baked Ham has nothing on this recipe!

I switched up this recipe quite a bit but it came out fabulous. I used dark brown sugar , cutie juice, honey and about a table spoon full of jim beam. Combined all ingredients in a small pot, whisked it all together until the sugar dissolved and let it come to a boil. Taste it and if it has too much liquor in it add more cutie juice and honey.

Excellent basic recipe. I added 1/2 tsp of cinnamon and 1/4 tsp of cloves (I would have added more of both, but my daughter prefers very sweet ham sauce). I only had 1/3 cup of honey, so I used maple syrup to make up the rest. 
I put all the ingredients in a saucepan and heated them to a boil, then glazed my ham every thirty minutes. I saved the rest to use as a sauce. 
I'm so glad I found this; I've been making hit-or-miss glazes for the last ten years.

Wonderful and so simple -- an excellent base! Leaves plenty of room for creativity. I changed it up a bit, and added 1/4 cup pineapple juice and 1/4 cup of orange juice, instead of a 1/2 cup of orange juice. I also added 3 tsp hot sweet mustard, about 1/4 tsp of ground ginger and about a TBS of grated orange peel. The pan gravy tasted so good with this glaze!

The only change made, due to the absence of oranges, I opened a can of pineapple slices, drained it, then squished half of it. Mixed all three ingredients very well, then bathed two cooked ham pieces, half an inch width in the sauce, the the halfmoon slices fit in the big sized pan after spraying pam though it was as teffal. Flipped each on both sides twice. Few minutes later we enjoyed the meal next to a side dish. Thank you.
Followed the basic recipe. I however did not have enough honey and added a tablespoon of molasses. I also added a 1/8 teaspoon of ground cloves. Would highly recommend this recipe.

I hate ham, but my mother-in-law ordered me to make one for Easter dinner (we had it a day early this year). I bought a Costco pre-cooked and pre-sliced ham and used this glaze instead of the one that came in the package with the ham. I made extra glaze and was very, very generous with the glaze when cooking, and also put some out on the table so people could put extra glaze on their ham, if desired (I can only tolerate ham when it has tons of yummy glaze to cover up the hammy taste). OMG -- the ham was DELICIOUS. Everyone commented about how good it was, and my husband said it was better than Honey Baked Ham. This is my new favorite main course to serve when entertaining since it is so darn easy and stress-free.

Overall this is a good recipe. At first the honey and OJ were kind of strong. I lightly dusted the mixture with ground clove & cinnamon. Still the orange & honey a bit much for me. I cooked it down to thicken it so it sticks to the ham steaks. Cooking it down to thicken it also blended the flavors beautifully! It's a bit sweet & I will use this again.
Only difference was I used Pineapple juices

OMG this was awesome I'm not the greatest cook in the kitchen but I did well I mean 3 ingredients who can mess that up I'm single so I only buy ham steaks I did add the clove and cinnamon just for the nostalgia and the taste was awesome 👍

Had an Easter ham in my freezer decided to make today. Puree’d two small small naval oranges and strained. One cup brown sugar, used what honey I had, made up the difference with molasses and added a shot of apple cider vinegar.
It worked for me. Had some leftover ham from easter and needed a glaze. I preferred a little less honey. Really easy to make.
I covered my ham in crushed pineapple before glazing my ham with this recipe. Turned out amazing, Thanks from all of us!
This glaze gave my ham such a fresh and delicious flavor and it was so easy to make. I also brushed it over the ham before cooking and basted it throughout. So good!

This was delicious. I was a little scant on juice which just helped the glaze stick to the ham better. I also added a decent amount of ground clove which gives such a nice flavor to the ham (if you like Trader Joe’s ham glaze, ground cloves are the prominent flavor).

This is excellent! I added spices - cloves, cardamom, cinnamon, and doubled it, because I wanted a thick glaze. I have used this twice on uncured hams for Easter and Christmas and it was delicious both times.
